description: Days used only in combined programmes. An integration day is added when both technologies are requested; a capstone is used when every requested technology is in its applies_to list.

day.topic: Python on AWS: Automation with boto3 and Lambda
subtopics: Credentials from roles instead of keys
Writing a Lambda handler in Python
day.lab_task: Write a Python Lambda function with boto3 that resizes images uploaded to S3 and records metadata in DynamoDB, with unit tests that mock AWS using moto.
day.deliverable: Function code, Lambda layer, IAM policy and passing tests
checks: Upload a test image to the input bucket
Resized image and a metadata item are created
Run the unit tests with the network off
Remove the role's DynamoDB permission and upload again
Function logs a ClientError with AccessDenied and does not crash
objectives: Automate AWS from Python with boto3
Build and test Python Lambda functions
Handle AWS errors and permissions in code

day.topic: Python on Azure: Azure SDK and Azure Functions
subtopics: Azure SDK for Python client libraries
Writing an Azure Function in Python
Bindings in the Python v2 programming model
Least-privilege role assignments for Python code
day.lab_task: Write a Python Azure Function that resizes images uploaded to Blob Storage and writes metadata to Table Storage, authenticating with managed identity, with unit tests that mock the SDK.
day.deliverable: Function code, role assignments and passing tests
checks: Upload a test image to the input container
Resized image and a metadata row are created
Search the code and settings for storage keys
Remove the identity's role and upload again
Function logs an authorisation error and does not crash
objectives: Automate Azure from Python with the Azure SDK
Build and test Python Azure Functions
Authenticate Python code with managed identity

day.topic: AWS and Azure Compared: Service Mapping and Multi-Cloud Decisions
subtopics: Mapping core services between AWS and Azure
Identity: IAM compared with Entra ID and Azure RBAC
When multi-cloud helps and when it adds risk
day.lab_task: Deploy the same small container web service on AWS (ECS Fargate) and Azure (Container Apps) with Terraform, then compare setup effort, monthly cost and operational differences.
day.deliverable: Terraform code for both clouds, a service mapping table and a one-page comparison with a recommendation
checks: Same service responds on AWS and Azure
Monthly cost for both uses the official calculators with the same assumptions
Choice is justified with at least three criteria
objectives: Map AWS and Azure services to each other
Compare clouds on cost and operations with evidence

day.deliverable: Helm chart, mapping table from Compose to Kubernetes and a running deployment
checks: Open the app through the cluster ingress
Every Compose setting has its Kubernetes equivalent or a reason
objectives: Keep health, limits, secrets and data during the move

day.deliverable: Terraform repository, plan and apply outputs and the running service URL
checks: App responds and reads from RDS
Search the code for AWS keys or the database password

day.deliverable: Terraform repository, plan and apply outputs and the running service URL

day.lab_task: Build, scan and publish multi-platform images from GitHub Actions with layer caching, SARIF results and provenance attestations, pushing only from main.

day.topic: GitHub Actions to Kubernetes: Deploy with Rollout Checks

No cluster credentials stored; OIDC is used

day.topic: Git Workflow Meets CI: Branch Protection, Checks and Merge Queues
day.lab_task: Protect main with required workflow checks and code owner reviews, add a merge queue, and automate versioned releases from Conventional Commits.
day.deliverable: Ruleset configuration, merge queue run and an automated release
checks: Merge a pull request with failing checks
Add two pull requests to the merge queue
Both are tested together and merged in order
objectives: Connect Git workflows to CI checks
Keep main green with merge queues

day.topic: Python with SQL Databases: Parameterised Queries, pandas and SQLAlchemy Core
subtopics: Connecting with psycopg and connection strings from the environment
Bulk loading with COPY from Python
Reading query results into pandas with read_sql
Testing database code against a container
day.lab_task: Write a Python script that loads a CSV of orders into PostgreSQL with COPY, runs parameterised report queries, loads the results into pandas for a chart and is tested against a database container.
day.deliverable: Script, report chart and passing tests
checks: Pass a customer name containing a quote and OR 1=1
Treated as text and returns no extra rows
Load 100,000 rows with COPY and with single inserts
COPY is at least ten times faster
Transaction rolls back and the table is unchanged
objectives: Use SQL databases safely from Python
Move data efficiently between Python and SQL

day.topic: Java with SQL: JDBC Transactions, Batching and Reading Plans from the Application
subtopics: Running EXPLAIN for queries the application sends
Fixing a slow query found in the application log
day.lab_task: Add an order import to a Java service with batched JDBC inserts in one transaction, log every SQL statement with its time, find the slowest report query and fix it with an index chosen from its plan.
day.deliverable: Import code, SQL log, plans before and after and timings
checks: Finishes at least five times faster than row by row
Throw an exception after half the rows
Slow report query plan changes to an index scan
objectives: Find slow SQL from the application

day.topic: Go with SQL: pgx, sqlc and Connection Pool Tuning
subtopics: Batch queries and COPY with pgx
day.lab_task: Build a Go report service that runs sqlc-generated queries through a tuned pgx pool with per-query timeouts, bulk-loads data with COPY and exposes pool metrics, then fix the slowest query.
day.deliverable: Service code, pool metrics and query timings
checks: Run 500 concurrent requests with a pool of 20
No connection errors and pool wait time reported
Run a query longer than its context timeout
Cancelled on the server as well as the client
objectives: Use pgx and sqlc in Go services

day.topic: TypeScript with SQL: Type-Safe Queries with Kysely and Migrations
subtopics: Kysely query builder and generated database types
Raw SQL with the sql template tag

day.deliverable: Typed query module, migration and tests
checks: Rename a column and regenerate types
Queries using the old name fail to compile
Pass an injection string as a parameter
objectives: Keep queries in step with the schema

day.topic: Java on AWS: SDK for Java 2.x, Lambda and SnapStart

day.deliverable: Function code, tests and cold start comparison
checks: Upload a file to the input bucket
Compare cold starts with SnapStart on and off
SnapStart cold start is clearly shorter
Run the tests with no internet
objectives: Use AWS from Java with SDK 2.x
Build and tune Java Lambda functions

day.topic: SQL on AWS: RDS, Aurora and Athena

day.deliverable: Cluster configuration, restore record, Performance Insights screenshot and Athena queries
checks: Send a read query to the reader endpoint
Restore to five minutes before a deleted row
Row is present in the restored cluster
Scanned bytes are a small fraction of the full table
objectives: Query data in S3 with SQL

day.deliverable: Configuration, failover test record and Query Store screenshots
checks: Force the earlier plan in Query Store
objectives: Secure and fail over managed databases
Fix plan regressions with Query Store

day.topic: S/4HANA Finance End to End: From Logistics Postings to the Universal Journal

Reconcile margin analysis with the G/L
